frequency_question: How often does a standalone, highly partisan voting reform or restriction bill successfully pass the U.S. Senate?
membership_rule: Includes major standalone bills specifically targeting voter registration rules, ID requirements, or federal election administration; excludes provisions bundled into must-pass omnibus bills, budget reconciliations, or procedural resolutions.

cases.name: Freedom to Vote Act / For the People Act (S.1)
Help America Vote Act (HAVA) reforms / specific amendments
National Voter Registration Act (NVRA) amendments or repeal attempts

provenance_note: 3 cases named, 5 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.7x); rate of 0% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 major named standalone attempts; all failed to clear the Senate threshold for passage.
known_gaps: Minor technical corrections bills pass frequently by unanimous consent, but major voter eligibility bills do not.
skeleton: Standalone partisan election bills considered in the Senate since 1994
multiplier: 0 out of roughly 5 major attempts passing as standalone bills due to filibuster thresholds and polarization
validity_reason: Valid until the conclusion of the current congressional makeup and potential rule changes regarding the filibuster.
